result: This manuscript describes a registered report for the Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology, which aims to replicate key experiments from a 2011 Nature paper by Dawson et al. on BET inhibition in MLL-fusion leukemia. Papers were selected based on citations and Altmetric scores from publications between 2010-2012.
evaluation: Claims C1-C4 provide clear methodological context for the replication study. These are straightforward descriptive claims about the project's purpose and paper selection criteria, supported by appropriate citations (Errington et al., 2014; Dawson et al., 2011).

result: MLL is a histone methyltransferase that undergoes chromosomal translocations, fusing with over 60 partners (commonly in super elongation complexes), converting it into a potent transcriptional activator that causes aggressive hematological malignancies with poor prognosis.
evaluation: Claims C10-C15 provide well-established background on MLL biology, supported by multiple appropriate citations (Marschalek, 2010; Meyer et al., 2009; Smith et al., 2011; Mueller et al., 2009; Slany, 2009; Tamai and Inokuchi, 2010). This represents standard knowledge in the field.

result: BET proteins are transcriptional regulators controlling cell cycle, growth, and inflammation genes. Dawson et al. identified novel BRD3/BRD4 interactions with SEC and PAF complexes in MLL-fusion cells and developed I-BET151, a BET inhibitor that prevents binding to acetylated histones.
evaluation: Claims C16-C19 describe established BET protein biology and the original study's findings, supported by appropriate citations. The logical inference in C17 follows reasonably from C16's description of BET protein function.

result: The original study demonstrated that I-BET151 selectively suppressed growth of MLL-fusion leukemia cell lines (MV4;11, RS4;11, MOLM13, NOMO1) with nanomolar IC50 values, while cell lines with other oncogenic drivers showed resistance (K526) or reduced sensitivity (HEL, HL60, MEG01) with micromolar IC50 values.
evaluation: Claims C5, C6, C20, and C21 accurately describe findings from the original Dawson et al. 2011 study that will be replicated in Protocol 2. These are appropriately cited claims about prior work that establish the rationale for replication.

result: Subsequent studies showed I-BET151 inhibits growth in multiple hematological malignancies (AML, multiple myeloma, primary effusion lymphoma) and solid tumors (medulloblastoma, melanoma, glioblastoma) at 100-500 nM. The BET inhibitor JQ1 showed similar selective activity against MV4;11 but not K526 cells.
evaluation: Claims C22-C26 describe follow-up studies with appropriate citations (Dawson et al., 2014; Chaidos et al., 2014; Tolani et al., 2014; Gallagher et al., 2014; Long et al., 2014; Pastori et al., 2014; Zuber et al., 2011). These provide important context for the broader significance of BET inhibition.

result: The original study showed I-BET151 transcriptionally downregulated the anti-apoptotic gene BCL-2 in MLL-fusion cell lines (MOLM13, MV4;11, NOMO1) but not in resistant K526 cells. This effect was also observed in AML patient samples with enhanced apoptosis.
evaluation: Claims C7, C27-C29 describe the original study's mechanistic findings regarding BCL-2 suppression, which will be replicated in Protocol 3. The claims are appropriately cited and provide clear rationale for the proposed replication experiments.

result: In contrast to MLL-fusion cells, I-BET151 promoted cell death/growth inhibition in HEL cells, Me1007 melanoma cells, and Sufu−/− cells without significantly impacting Bcl-2 gene or protein expression, indicating alternative mechanisms of action.
evaluation: Claims C30-C32 describe important context from other studies (Wyspianska et al., 2014; Gallagher et al., 2014; Long et al., 2014) showing that BCL-2 suppression is not universal across all I-BET151-sensitive cell types, highlighting the specificity of the MLL-fusion mechanism.

result: In vivo studies demonstrated that I-BET151 significantly improved disease-free survival and reduced peripheral blood disease in MLL-fusion leukemia xenograft models. Similar tumor suppression was observed in other xenograft models, and JQ1 showed comparable efficacy in AML and multiple myeloma xenografts.
evaluation: Claims C8, C9, C33-C36 describe in vivo efficacy findings from the original study and related work, supported by appropriate citations. These establish the therapeutic potential that will be tested in Protocols 4 and 5.

result: Protocol 1 will empirically determine cell doubling times, which are assumed to be approximately 25 hours for K-562 cells and 50 hours for MV4;11 cells, to establish appropriate treatment durations for Protocol 2.
evaluation: Claims C37-C38 describe reasonable assumptions that will be empirically tested in Protocol 1. The protocol appropriately plans to verify these assumptions rather than relying on literature values, which is good experimental practice.

result: The replication will use busulfan conditioning instead of the original study's 300 cGy radiation, based on literature showing comparable efficacy for human cell engraftment in NOD-SCID mice. The original study used 30 mg/kg/day I-BET151, but MTD will be reassessed due to batch-to-batch variation.
evaluation: Claims C39-C41 describe a justified methodological modification (busulfan vs. radiation) supported by citation (Robert-Richard et al., 2006) and a prudent safety measure (MTD reassessment). These are reasonable adaptations for the replication study.

result: In the original study, two mice were censored from the I-BET151 cohort during the 21-day treatment period, which is incorporated into the power calculations for Protocol 5 by adjusting the censoring rate.
evaluation: Claim C49 accurately reports censoring information from the original study and appropriately incorporates this into power calculations. The protocol plans for 14 mice per group to account for potential higher censoring rates, which is methodologically sound.
